scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4630: HELP! One of the lab workstations has turned into a
complete BRICK. It can't reach anything at all, not even its own gateway
thing. Something around the hole it plugs into must be wrong, but I don't know
what. Could someone move it to a working port and make it talk to the network
again!! The student who uses it is just sitting there!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. it_lab3 has its IP on 192.168.1.0/24, reaches its
  gateway (192.168.1.1) with 0% loss, and RIP is converged so it reaches other
  segments too. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a single-host isolation that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- it_lab3 is totally isolated
and cannot reach even its gateway -- is NOT reproducible: it_lab3 holds its
192.168.1.0/24 address, reaches its default gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss, and
(RIP being converged on router0/router1/router2) reaches off-segment destinations as
well.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: it_lab3 is fully connected and the user's
report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the it_lab3 -> gateway path
(and an off-segment ping), finds it working, checks the host's interface/route, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dead port or isolated host to satisfy the
ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I tested every lab workstation segment end-to-end. All IT lab hosts (it_lab1–it_lab4) have valid IPs in 192.168.1.0/24 with default via 192.168.1.1 and can ping their own gateway with 0% loss (e.g., it_lab1→192.168.1.1 avg ~0.96 ms). All CS lab hosts (cs_lab1–cs_lab4) have valid IPs in 192.168.2.0/24 with default via 192.168.2.1 and also reach their gateway with 0% loss (e.g., cs_lab1→192.168.2.1 avg ~1.44 ms). Router0’s interfaces (eth0=192.168.1.1, eth1=192.168.2.1) are UP/LOWER_UP and respond to hosts. Switch0 (IT) and Switch1 (CS) show both uplink (eth0) and user-facing (eth1) ports UP and bridged (br0) with RX/TX counters incrementing, indicating healthy L2 forwarding. Other VLANs/segments similarly reach their gateways.

Mechanistically, a host that “can’t reach anything, not even the gateway” would typically have a local link issue (down NIC/cable/jack) or a misconfigured IP. None of those conditions are present on any modeled lab workstation; the behavior is not reproducible on the network side.

Localization: no faults found on router0 eth0/eth1, switch0, or switch1; all lab hosts’ eth0 links are up with valid routes.

Root cause: No network-side fault detected; the reported symptom likely stems from a physical port/cable or NIC issue at that specific seat, outside the simulated infrastructure.

Corrective fix: Move the workstation to a known-good jack/patch lead, reseat/replace the cable, verify link LED and that eth0 is up, and confirm correct IP/gateway settings. If the issue follows the PC, check/replace its NIC.
